A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArbInterp work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original interpolation comparisons, component and training-stage ablations, 256x evaluation, and generated-frame examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a controlled motion-transfer experiment in Appendix C.2 and Figure 10.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 adds a dedicated reconstruction model conditioned on the first frame and Motion Semantic Extractor features for motion-transfer testing. This is a limited auxiliary adaptation; the main ArbInterp architecture, TaRoPE, losses, and interpolation procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds a controlled motion-transfer scenario that changes first-frame appearance while retaining source-video motion information. The training datasets, MultiInterpBench coverage, streaming interpolation, and 256x evaluation were already present in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain LDMVFI, TRF, GI, DynamiCrafter, and ArbInterp-SVD in Tables 1 and 3. Component comparisons in Table 2 are also unchanged; the new motion-transfer example introduces no competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a reconstruction-training and testing protocol: extract source-video motion, edit the conditioning first frame, and assess motion preservation while retaining the extracted features. Settings, metrics, sample counts, and training budgets for existing experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix C.2 and Figure 10 directly probe appearance–motion separation through controlled appearance editing, supplementing v1's component ablations. Existing timestamp, training-stage, streaming, and beyond-training-range analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 256x subclip-averaging procedure is unchanged, and the new qualitative experiment adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including ArbInterp's 32x FVD of 319.9. Figure 10 adds qualitative results reporting preserved motion after appearance editing; the relocated streaming examples are retained results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the RoPE and timestamp definitions, training-loss formulations, and interpolation-complexity argument are unchanged. No new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The core claims about arbitrary timestamps and lengths, appearance–motion conditioning, and interpolation performance retain their meaning. The streaming-coherence novelty claim in v2 Section 4.5 already appeared in v1 Appendix C.1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets motion preservation under appearance editing as evidence that the MSE separates motion from appearance to a considerable extent. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning text control, model/data scale, and complex scenes.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B and Table 5 retain the same implementation details, optimizer, hardware, preprocessing, training schedules, and resource links. The new diagnostic describes its experimental setup without adding specific implementation parameters or access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds citations to Li et al. (2025, 2026), listed as MixGRPO and UniF2ace, in the temporal-indexing discussion. The related-work taxonomy and broader contribution positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, expands the arbitrary-time explanation, and corrects its figure reference from Figure 9 to Figure 7. It moves streaming interpolation from Appendix C.1 to Section 4.5 and adds acknowledgments and conference-publication headers.

P2.justification: v2 adds the controlled-motion-transfer Figure 10, moves and enlarges v1's streaming Figure 9 as main-text Figure 8, and resizes several diagrams. Other figures are retained with renumbering or reflow, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.2 and Figure 10 add a useful appearance-intervention check supporting motion separation beyond v1's ablations. The corrected figure reference and integrated streaming discussion improve readability. The gain is limited because the new evidence is qualitative and uses a separately trained model with sparse implementation detail; quantitative validation is unchanged.
